1	# Templating
2	
3	`standout-render` uses a two-pass templating system that combines a template engine for logic and data binding with a custom BBCode-like syntax for styling. This separation keeps templates readable while providing full control over both content and presentation.
4	
5	The default engine is MiniJinja (Jinja2-compatible), but alternative engines are available. See [Template Engines](template-engines.md) for options including a lightweight `SimpleEngine` for reduced binary size.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Two-Pass Rendering Pipeline
10	
11	Templates are processed in two distinct passes:
12	
13	```text
14	Template + Data → [Pass 1: MiniJinja] → Text with style tags → [Pass 2: BBParser] → Final output
15	```
16	
17	**Pass 1 - MiniJinja**: Standard template processing. Variables are substituted, control flow executes, filters apply.
18	
19	**Pass 2 - BBParser**: Style tag processing. Bracket-notation tags are converted to ANSI escape codes (or stripped, depending on output mode).
20	
21	### Pipeline Example
22	
23	```text
24	Template:     [title]{{ name }}[/title] has {{ count }} items
25	Data:         { name: "Report", count: 42 }
26	
27	After Pass 1: [title]Report[/title] has 42 items
28	After Pass 2: \x1b[1;36mReport\x1b[0m has 42 items  (or plain: "Report has 42 items")
29	```
30	
31	This separation means:
32	
33	- Template logic (loops, conditionals) is handled by MiniJinja—a mature, well-documented engine
34	- Style application is a simple, predictable transformation
35	- You can debug each pass independently
36	
37	---
38	
39	## MiniJinja Basics
40	
41	MiniJinja implements Jinja2 syntax, a widely-used templating language. Here's a quick overview:
42	
43	### Variables
44	
45	```jinja
46	{{ variable }}
47	{{ object.field }}
48	{{ list[0] }}
49	```
50	
51	### Control Flow
52	
53	```jinja
54	{% if condition %}
55	  Show this
56	{% elif other_condition %}
57	  Show that
58	{% else %}
59	  Default
60	{% endif %}
61	
62	{% for item in items %}
63	  {{ loop.index }}. {{ item.name }}
64	{% endfor %}
65	```
66	
67	### Filters
68	
69	```jinja
70	{{ name | upper }}
71	{{ list | length }}
72	{{ value | default("N/A") }}
73	{{ text | truncate(20) }}
74	```
75	
76	### Comments
77	
78	```jinja
79	{# This is a comment and won't appear in output #}
80	```
81	
82	For comprehensive MiniJinja documentation, see the [MiniJinja documentation](https://docs.rs/minijinja).
83	
84	### Booleans and None
85	
86	Standout renders these the Rust way — `true`, `false`, `none` — not the Jinja2
87	way MiniJinja itself uses (`True`, `False`, `None`). This holds for
88	interpolation, loop and `set` bindings, `| string`, `| join`, sequence and map
89	literals, standout's own filters, and table cells:
90	
91	```jinja
92	{{ flag }}                {# true #}
93	{{ missing }}             {# none #}
94	{{ flags }}               {# [true, false, none] #}
95	{{ flags | join(", ") }}  {# true, false, none #}
96	```
97	
98	Two exceptions:
99	
100	- The `~` concatenation operator formats inside MiniJinja's evaluator, which
101	  exposes no hook: `{{ "x" ~ flag }}` yields `xTrue`. Write `{{ "x" }}{{ flag }}`
102	  or `{{ "x" ~ flag | string }}`.
103	- Structured output (JSON, YAML, XML, CSV) skips templates entirely and
104	  serializes your data directly, so those modes follow their format's own rules.
105	
106	If you build a `minijinja::Environment` yourself, use
107	`standout_render::template::new_environment()` — or call `register_filters` on
108	your own environment, which installs the same spelling.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## The Trailing-Newline Contract
113	
114	Two things happen to the newline at the end of a template, and together they
115	are observable in the bytes a script reads, so they are stated here rather than
116	discovered by probing.
117	
118	**The engine consumes exactly one final newline.** This is Jinja's rule and
119	MiniJinja keeps it. A template file ending in a single `\n` renders with no
120	trailing newline at all; a file ending in two renders with one.
121	
122	| Template source | Rendered string |
123	| --- | --- |
124	| `{{ name }}` | `x` |
125	| `{{ name }}\n` | `x` |
126	| `{{ name }}\n\n` | `x\n` |
127	| `{{ name }}\n\n\n` | `x\n\n` |
128	
129	**The process edge appends exactly one newline.** `App::run` writes a handled
130	command's text with `writeln!`, so what reaches stdout is the rendered string
131	plus one `\n` — whatever the template ended with.
132	
133	The practical consequence: a template that ends with one newline and a template
134	that ends with none produce identical bytes. To end a page with a blank line,
135	the template needs *two* trailing newlines. Every editor that adds a final
136	newline on save is therefore invisible here, which is the reason the rule is
137	worth stating.
138	
139	`standout-render/tests/trailing_newline.rs` pins the engine half;
140	`final_emission_routes_success_and_diagnostics_to_distinct_streams` in
141	`standout/src/cli/builder/execution.rs` pins the process half.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Style Tags
146	
147	Style tags use BBCode-like bracket notation to apply named styles from your theme:
148	
149	```jinja
150	[style-name]content to style[/style-name]
151	```
152	
153	### Basic Usage
154	
155	```jinja
156	[title]Report Summary[/title]
157	[error]Something went wrong![/error]
158	[muted]Last updated: {{ timestamp }}[/muted]
159	```
160	
161	### Nesting
162	
163	Tags can nest properly:
164	
165	```jinja
166	[outer][inner]nested content[/inner][/outer]
167	```
168	
169	### Spanning Lines
170	
171	Tags can span multiple lines:
172	
173	```jinja
174	[panel]
175	This is a multi-line
176	block of styled content
177	[/panel]
178	```
179	
180	### With Template Logic
181	
182	Style tags and MiniJinja work together seamlessly:
183	
184	```jinja
185	[title]{% if custom_title %}{{ custom_title }}{% else %}Default Title{% endif %}[/title]
186	
187	{% for task in tasks %}
188	[{{ task.status }}]{{ task.title }}[/{{ task.status }}]
189	{% endfor %}
190	```
191	
192	The second example shows dynamic style names—the style applied depends on the value of `task.status`.
193	
194	---
195	
196	## Processing Modes
197	
198	Pass 2 (BBParser) processes style tags differently based on the output mode:
199	
200	| Mode | Behavior | Use Case |
201	| ------ | ---------- | ---------- |
202	| `Term` | Replace tags with ANSI escape codes | Rich terminal output |
203	| `Text` | Strip tags completely | Plain text, pipes, files |
204	| `TermDebug` | Keep tags as literal text | Debugging, testing |
205	
206	### Processing Modes Example
207	
208	Template: `[title]Hello[/title]`
209	
210	- **Term**: `\x1b[1;36mHello\x1b[0m` (rendered as cyan bold)
211	- **Text**: `Hello`
212	- **TermDebug**: `[title]Hello[/title]`
213	
214	### Setting the Mode
215	
216	```rust
217	use standout_render::{render_with_output, OutputMode};
218	
219	// Rich terminal
220	let output = render_with_output(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Term)?;
221	
222	// Plain text
223	let output = render_with_output(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Text)?;
224	
225	// Debug (tags visible)
226	let output = render_with_output(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::TermDebug)?;
227	
228	// Auto-detect based on TTY
229	let output = render_with_output(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Auto)?;
230	```
231	
232	### Auto Mode
233	
234	`OutputMode::Auto` detects the appropriate mode:
235	
236	- If stdout is a TTY with color support → `Term`
237	- If stdout is a pipe or redirect → `Text`
238	
239	> **For standout framework users:** The framework's `--output` CLI flag automatically sets the output mode. See standout documentation for details.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Built-in Filters
244	
245	Beyond MiniJinja's standard filters, `standout-render` provides formatting filters:
246	
247	### Column Formatting
248	
249	```jinja
250	{{ value | col(10) }}                              {# pad/truncate to 10 chars #}
251	{{ value | col(20, align="right") }}               {# right-align in 20 chars #}
252	{{ value | col(15, truncate="middle") }}           {# truncate in middle #}
253	{{ value | col(15, truncate="start", ellipsis="...") }}
254	```
255	
256	### Padding
257	
258	```jinja
259	{{ "42" | pad_left(8) }}      {# "      42" #}
260	{{ "hi" | pad_right(8) }}     {# "hi      " #}
261	{{ "hi" | pad_center(8) }}    {# "   hi   " #}
262	```
263	
264	### Truncation
265	
266	```jinja
267	{{ long_text | truncate_at(20) }}                   {# "Very long text th..." #}
268	{{ path | truncate_at(30, "middle", "...") }}      {# "/home/.../file.txt" #}
269	{{ text | truncate_at(20, "start") }}              {# "...end of the text" #}
270	```
271	
272	### Display Width
273	
274	```jinja
275	{% if value | display_width > 20 %}
276	  {{ value | truncate_at(20) }}
277	{% else %}
278	  {{ value }}
279	{% endif %}
280	```
281	
282	Returns visual width (handles Unicode—CJK characters count as 2).
283	
284	### Style Application
285	
286	```jinja
287	{{ value | style_as("error") }}                    {# wraps in [error]...[/error] #}
288	{{ task.status | style_as(task.status) }}         {# dynamic: [pending]pending[/pending] #}
289	```
290	
291	---
292	
293	## Template Registry
294	
295	When using the `Renderer` struct, templates are resolved by name through a registry:
296	
297	```rust
298	use standout_render::Renderer;
299	
300	let mut renderer = Renderer::new(theme)?;
301	
302	// Add inline template
303	renderer.add_template("greeting", "Hello, [name]{{ name }}[/name]!")?;
304	
305	// Add directory of templates
306	renderer.add_template_dir("./templates")?;
307	
308	// Render by name
309	let output = renderer.render("greeting", &data)?;
310	```
311	
312	### Resolution Priority
313	
314	1. **Inline templates** (added via `add_template()`)
315	2. **Directory templates** (from `add_template_dir()`)
316	
317	### File Extensions
318	
319	Supported extensions (in priority order): `.jinja`, `.jinja2`, `.j2`, `.stpl`, `.txt`
320	
321	When you request `"report"`, the registry checks:
322	
323	- Inline template named `"report"`
324	- `report.jinja` in registered directories
325	- `report.jinja2`, `report.j2`, `report.stpl`, `report.txt` (lower priority)
326	
327	The `.stpl` extension is for SimpleEngine templates. See [Template Engines](template-engines.md) for details.
328	
329	### Template Names
330	
331	Template names are derived from relative paths:
332	
333	```text
334	templates/
335	├── greeting.jinja       → "greeting"
336	├── reports/
337	│   └── summary.jinja    → "reports/summary"
338	└── errors/
339	    └── 404.jinja        → "errors/404"
340	```
341	
342	---
343	
344	## Including Templates
345	
346	Templates can include other templates using MiniJinja's include syntax:
347	
348	```jinja
349	{# main.jinja #}
350	[title]{{ title }}[/title]
351	
352	{% include "partials/header.jinja" %}
353	
354	{% for item in items %}
355	  {% include "partials/item.jinja" %}
356	{% endfor %}
357	
358	{% include "partials/footer.jinja" %}
359	```
360	
361	This enables reusable components across your application.
362	
363	---
364	
365	## Context Variables
366	
367	Beyond your data, you can inject additional context into templates:
368	
369	```rust
370	use standout_render::{render_with_vars, OutputMode};
371	use std::collections::HashMap;
372	
373	let mut vars = HashMap::new();
374	vars.insert("version", "1.0.0");
375	vars.insert("app_name", "MyApp");
376	
377	let output = render_with_vars(
378	    "{{ app_name }} v{{ version }}: {{ message }}",
379	    &data,
380	    &theme,
381	    OutputMode::Term,
382	    vars,
383	)?;
384	```
385	
386	When handler data and context variables have the same key, **handler data wins**. Context is supplementary.
387	
388	---
389	
390	## Structured Output
391	
392	For machine-readable output (JSON, YAML, CSV), templates are bypassed entirely:
393	
394	```rust
395	use standout_render::{render_auto, OutputMode};
396	
397	// Template is used for Term/Text modes
398	// Data is serialized directly for Json/Yaml/Csv
399	let output = render_auto(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Json)?;
400	```
401	
402	| Mode | Behavior |
403	| ------ | ---------- |
404	| `Term` | Render template, apply styles |
405	| `Text` | Render template, strip styles |
406	| `TermDebug` | Render template, keep style tags |
407	| `Json` | `serde_json::to_string_pretty(data)` |
408	| `Yaml` | `serde_yaml::to_string(data)` |
409	| `Csv` | Flatten and format as CSV |
410	
411	This means your serializable data types automatically support structured output without additional code.
412	
413	---
414	
415	## Validation
416	
417	Check templates for unknown style tags before deploying:
418	
419	```rust
420	use standout_render::validate_template;
421	
422	let errors = validate_template(template, &sample_data, &theme);
423	if !errors.is_empty() {
424	    for error in &errors {
425	        eprintln!("Unknown style tag: [{}]", error.tag_name);
426	    }
427	}
428	```
429	
430	Validation catches:
431	
432	- Misspelled style names
433	- References to undefined styles
434	- Mismatched opening/closing tags
435	
436	---
437	
438	## API Reference
439	
440	### Render Functions
441	
442	```rust
443	use standout_render::{
444	    render,                  // Basic: template + data + theme
445	    render_with_output,      // With explicit output mode
446	    render_with_mode,        // With output mode + color mode
447	    render_with_vars,        // With extra context variables
448	    render_auto,             // Auto-dispatch template vs serialize
449	    render_auto_with_context,
450	};
451	
452	// Basic
453	let output = render(template, &data, &theme)?;
454	
455	// With output mode
456	let output = render_with_output(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Term)?;
457	
458	// With color mode override (for testing)
459	let output = render_with_mode(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Term, ColorMode::Dark)?;
460	
461	// Auto (template for text modes, serialize for structured)
462	let output = render_auto(template, &data, &theme, OutputMode::Json)?;
463	```
464	
465	### Renderer Struct
466	
467	```rust
468	use standout_render::Renderer;
469	
470	let mut renderer = Renderer::new(theme)?;
471	renderer.add_template("name", "content")?;
472	renderer.add_template_dir("./templates")?;
473	
474	let output = renderer.render("name", &data)?;
475	let output = renderer.render_with_mode("name", &data, OutputMode::Text)?;
476	```

202	`TargetProperties::detect()` is the one process probe, at the crate edge. Convenience wrappers call it then pass the result into `render_request`. Tests construct `TargetProperties` with an explicit `color_scheme` rather than installing a detector; `set_theme_detector` and the other detector override APIs are removed.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Style Aliasing
207	
208	Aliases let semantic names resolve to visual styles. This is useful when multiple concepts share the same appearance:
209	
210	```rust
211	let theme = Theme::new()
212	    // Define the visual style once
213	    .add("title", Style::new().bold().cyan())
214	    // Aliases — pass a string to reference another style by name
215	    .add("commit-message", "title")
216	    .add("section-header", "title")
217	    .add("heading", "title");
218	```
219	
220	Now `[commit-message]`, `[section-header]`, and `[heading]` all render identically to `[title]`.
221	
222	Benefits:
223	
224	- Templates use meaningful, context-specific names
225	- Visual changes propagate automatically
226	- Refactoring visual design doesn't touch templates
227	
228	Aliases can chain: `a` → `b` → `c` → concrete style. Cycles are detected and rejected at load time.
229	
230	---
231	
232	## Unknown Style Tags
233	
234	When a template references a style not defined in the theme, `standout-render` handles it gracefully:
235	
236	| Output Mode | Behavior                                                   |
237	| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
238	| `Term`      | Unknown tags get a `?` marker: `[unknown?]text[/unknown?]` |
239	| `Text`      | Tags stripped (plain text)                                 |
240	| `TermDebug` | Tags preserved as-is                                       |
241	
242	The `?` marker helps catch typos during development without crashing production apps.
243	
244	### Validation
245	
246	For strict checking at startup:
247	
248	```rust
249	use standout_render::validate_template;
250	
251	if let Err(error) = validate_template(template, &sample_data, &theme) {
252	    eprintln!("Unknown style tag: {}", error);
253	    std::process::exit(1);
254	}
255	```
256	
257	---
258	
259	## Built-in Styles
260	
261	`Theme::default()` includes adaptive styles for alternating table row backgrounds. These are used automatically when you pass `row_styles=true` (or a tint name) to the `table()` template function.
262	
263	| Style name              | Purpose                                 |
264	| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
265	| `table_row_even`        | Even rows — no background (transparent) |
266	| `table_row_odd`         | Odd rows — subtle gray background shift |
267	| `table_row_even_gray`   | Alias for `table_row_even`              |
268	| `table_row_odd_gray`    | Alias for `table_row_odd`               |
269	| `table_row_even_blue`   | Even rows for blue tint                 |
270	| `table_row_odd_blue`    | Odd rows — dark navy / lavender bg      |
271	| `table_row_even_red`    | Even rows for red tint                  |
272	| `table_row_odd_red`     | Odd rows — dark crimson / blush bg      |
273	| `table_row_even_green`  | Even rows for green tint                |
274	| `table_row_odd_green`   | Odd rows — dark forest / mint bg        |
275	| `table_row_even_purple` | Even rows for purple tint               |
276	| `table_row_odd_purple`  | Odd rows — dark plum / lilac bg         |
277	
278	All odd-row styles are adaptive: they resolve to a dark variant when the terminal is in dark mode, and a light variant in light mode. You can override any of these by defining the same style name in your theme.
279	
280	---
281	
282	## Best Practices
283	
284	### Semantic, Presentation, and Visual Layers
285	
286	Organize your styles in three conceptual layers:
287	
288	**1. Visual primitives** (low-level appearance):
289	
290	```css
291	._cyan-bold { color: cyan; font-weight: bold; }
292	._dim { opacity: 0.5; }
293	._red-bold { color: red; font-weight: bold; }
294	```
295	
296	**2. Presentation roles** (UI concepts — use aliases in code):
297	
298	```rust
299	theme.add("heading", "_cyan-bold")
300	     .add("secondary", "_dim")
301	     .add("danger", "_red-bold");
302	```
303	
304	**3. Semantic names** (domain concepts — aliases to presentation):
305	
306	```rust
307	// In templates, use these
308	theme.add("task-title", "heading")
309	     .add("task-status-done", "success")
310	     .add("task-status-pending", "warning")
311	     .add("error-message", "danger");
312	```
313	
314	Templates use semantic names (`task-title`), which resolve to presentation roles (`heading`), which resolve to visual primitives (`_cyan-bold`).
315	
316	This layering lets you:
317	
318	- Refactor visuals without touching templates
319	- Maintain consistency across domains

---

## Style Aliasing

Aliases let semantic names resolve to visual styles. This is useful when multiple concepts share the same appearance:

```rust
let theme = Theme::new()
    // Define the visual style once
    .add("title", Style::new().bold().cyan())
    // Aliases — pass a string to reference another style by name
    .add("commit-message", "title")
    .add("section-header", "title")

```

Now `[commit-message]`, `[section-header]`, and `[heading]` all render identically to `[title]`.

Benefits:

- Templates use meaningful, context-specific names

## Unknown Style Tags

| Output Mode | Behavior                                                   |

#!/bin/bash
# Black-box acceptance walk over SPEC.md. Not part of the deliverable.
B="$PWD/app/target/debug/gcloudlike"
ROOT="$PWD/.tmp"
pass=0; fail=0

reset() { rm -rf "$ROOT/cfg"; mkdir -p "$ROOT/cfg"; }

# check <label> <want-exit> <want-stdout> <want-stderr> -- cmd...
check() {
  local label=$1 wcode=$2 wout=$3 werr=$4; shift 5
  local out err code
  out=$("$@" 2>"$ROOT/e"); code=$?; err=$(cat "$ROOT/e")
  if [ "$code" = "$wcode" ] && [ "$out" = "$wout" ] && [ "$err" = "$werr" ]; then
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    fail=$((fail+1))
    echo "FAIL: $label"
    echo "  cmd:  $*"
    [ "$code" = "$wcode" ] || echo "  exit: want=$wcode got=$code"
    [ "$out" = "$wout" ] || { echo "  stdout want: |$wout|"; echo "  stdout got : |$out|"; }
    [ "$err" = "$werr" ] || { echo "  stderr want: |$werr|"; echo "  stderr got : |$err|"; }
  fi
}

unset GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_PROJECT GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_ACCOUNT GCLOUDLIKE_COMPUTE_ZONE GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG
export GCLOUDLIKE_CONFIG_DIR="$ROOT/cfg"
reset

## ---- inventory ---------------------------------------------------------
check "list alpha" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING
web-2 us-b2 small TERMINATED" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj
check "list beta" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
db-1 us-a1 large RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances list --project beta-proj
check "list narrowed by zone" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1
check "list narrowed to nothing" 0 "NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS" "" \
  -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone nowhere
check "list unknown project" 0 "NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS" "" \
  -- $B compute instances list --project ghost
check "list needs a project" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unset property: core/project" \
  -- $B compute instances list
check "account never filters" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING
web-2 us-b2 small TERMINATED" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --account who@example.com

check "describe" 0 \
"name: web-1
project: alpha-proj
zone: us-a1
machine_type: small
status: RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances describe web-1 --project alpha-proj
check "describe ignores zone" 0 \
"name: web-2
project: alpha-proj
zone: us-b2
machine_type: small
status: TERMINATED" "" -- $B compute instances describe web-2 --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1
check "describe foreign instance" 1 "" "gcloudlike: no such instance: db-1" \
  -- $B compute instances describe db-1 --project alpha-proj
check "describe unknown instance" 1 "" "gcloudlike: no such instance: nope" \
  -- $B compute instances describe nope --project alpha-proj
check "describe needs a project" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unset property: core/project" \
  -- $B compute instances describe web-1

## ---- effective value ---------------------------------------------------
reset
$B config set core/project from-set --quiet
check "value from the active set" 0 "from-set" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_PROJECT=from-env \
  check "env beats the set" 0 "from-env" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_PROJECT=from-env \
  check "flag beats env" 0 "from-flag" "" -- $B config get-value core/project --project from-flag
GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_PROJECT= \
  check "an empty variable is unset" 0 "from-set" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
check "unset property" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unset property: compute/zone" -- $B config get-value compute/zone
check "unknown property" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown property: core/nope" -- $B config get-value core/nope
check "unknown property, unknown section" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown property: nope/nope" \
  -- $B config get-value nope/nope

## ---- sets do not merge -------------------------------------------------
reset
$B config set core/project default-proj --quiet
$B config set core/account default-acct --quiet
$B config configurations create prod --quiet
$B --configuration prod config set core/project prod-proj --quiet
check "the active set applies whole" 0 "prod-proj" "" -- $B --configuration prod config get-value core/project
check "nothing leaks from default" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unset property: core/account" \
  -- $B --configuration prod config get-value core/account
check "default still has its own" 0 "default-acct" "" -- $B config get-value core/account

GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG=prod \
  check "the variable names a set" 0 "prod-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG= \
  check "an empty variable names none" 0 "default-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG=default \
  check "the flag beats the variable" 0 "prod-proj" "" -- $B --configuration prod config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_CORE_PROJECT=from-env \
  check "a flag naming a set does not outrank a variable supplying a property" 0 "from-env" "" \
  -- $B --configuration prod config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG=prod \
  check "a variable naming a set does not outrank a flag supplying one" 0 "from-flag" "" \
  -- $B config get-value core/project --project from-flag

$B config configurations activate prod --quiet
check "the active_config file names a set" 0 "prod-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG=default \
  check "the variable beats the file" 0 "default-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
check "unknown set from the flag" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown configuration: ghost" \
  -- $B --configuration ghost config list
GCLOUDLIKE_ACTIVE_CONFIG=ghost \
  check "unknown set from the variable" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown configuration: ghost" -- $B config list
printf 'ghost\n' > "$ROOT/cfg/active_config"
check "unknown set from the file" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown configuration: ghost" -- $B config list
rm -f "$ROOT/cfg/active_config"
check "an absent active_config means default" 0 "default-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project
printf '' > "$ROOT/cfg/active_config"
check "an empty active_config means default" 0 "default-proj" "" -- $B config get-value core/project

## ---- config list -------------------------------------------------------
reset
check "config list, nothing effective" 0 "" "" -- $B config list
$B config set core/project alpha-proj --quiet
check "one section" 0 \
"[core]
project = alpha-proj" "" -- $B config list
check "sections and properties ascend" 0 \
"[compute]
zone = us-a1
[core]
account = a@b
project = alpha-proj" "" -- $B config list --zone us-a1 --account a@b

## ---- config set --------------------------------------------------------
reset
mkdir -p "$ROOT/cfg/configurations"
printf '[other]\nkeep = me\n\n[core]\nproject = old\naccount = who\n' > "$ROOT/cfg/configurations/config_default"
check "set notice" 0 "" "Updated property [core/project]." -- $B config set core/project new
want=$'[other]\nkeep = me\n\n[core]\nproject = new\naccount = who\n'
got=$(cat "$ROOT/cfg/configurations/config_default")
if [ "$got" = "${want%$'\n'}" ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); else fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL: set rewrites one line"; echo "|$got|"; fi
check "set is quiet under --quiet" 0 "" "" -- $B config set core/project newer --quiet
check "set rejects an unknown property" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown property: core/nope" -- $B config set core/nope x
check "set rejects a malformed key" 2 "" "" -- $B config set nope x
check "set writes into the active set" 0 "" "Created [prod]." -- $B config configurations create prod
$B --configuration prod config set compute/zone us-b2 --quiet
check "the new set holds it" 0 "us-b2" "" -- $B --configuration prod config get-value compute/zone
check "the old set does not" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unset property: compute/zone" -- $B config get-value compute/zone

## ---- configurations ----------------------------------------------------
check "configurations list" 0 \
"NAME IS_ACTIVE
default True
prod False" "" -- $B config configurations list
check "create is not activate" 0 \
"NAME IS_ACTIVE
default True
prod False" "" -- $B config configurations list
check "create an existing set" 1 "" "gcloudlike: configuration already exists: prod" \
  -- $B config configurations create prod
check "create default" 1 "" "gcloudlike: configuration already exists: default" \
  -- $B config configurations create default
before=$(cat "$ROOT/cfg/configurations/config_prod")
$B config configurations create prod 2>/dev/null
after=$(cat "$ROOT/cfg/configurations/config_prod")
if [ "$before" = "$after" ]; then pass=$((pass+1)); else fail=$((fail+1)); echo "FAIL: a refused create writes nothing"; fi
check "activate" 0 "" "Activated [prod]." -- $B config configurations activate prod
check "activate persisted" 0 \
"NAME IS_ACTIVE
default False
prod True" "" -- $B config configurations list
check "activate is quiet under --quiet" 0 "" "" -- $B config configurations activate default
check "activate an unknown set" 1 "" "gcloudlike: unknown configuration: ghost" \
  -- $B config configurations activate ghost
check "create is quiet under --quiet" 0 "" "" -- $B config configurations create staging --quiet

## ---- forms -------------------------------------------------------------
reset
check "format json" 0 \
'{
  "instances": [
    {
      "name": "web-1",
      "zone": "us-a1",
      "machine_type": "small",
      "status": "RUNNING"
    }
  ]
}' "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1 --format json
check "output json" 0 \
'{
  "name": "web-1",
  "project": "alpha-proj",
  "zone": "us-a1",
  "machine_type": "small",
  "status": "RUNNING"
}' "" -- $B compute instances describe web-1 --project alpha-proj --output json
check "format json beats output text" 0 \
'{
  "instances": [
    {
      "name": "web-1",
      "zone": "us-a1",
      "machine_type": "small",
      "status": "RUNNING"
    }
  ]
}' "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1 --format json --output text
check "format text beats output json" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1 --format text --output json
check "output term does not change the text" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1 --format text --output term
check "output text" 0 \
"NAME ZONE MACHINE_TYPE STATUS
web-1 us-a1 small RUNNING" "" -- $B compute instances list --project alpha-proj --zone us-a1 --output text

check "a bad output is a usage error" 2 "" "" -- $B config list --output nope

check() {
  local pre=""
  case $1 in ENV:*) pre=${1#ENV:}; shift;; esac

  if [ -n "$pre" ]; then set -- env "$pre" "$@"; fi

check() {

#! standout-answers 1
#! questionnaire: corpus.exit
#! fingerprint: sha256:64291870245510dad73ca960fd4024db9b9c161113a3dcc9c7e57a30973663fc

1. Summarize what you built and what state it is in. (text) <id:summary>

`gcloudlike`, complete and working, in `app/`. `cargo build` and `cargo build
--release` are clean (the only warning is the sandbox's own `xcrun` cache
error, not the crate's).

Layout: `src/inventory.rs` (the three frozen rows), `src/settings.rs` (property
keys, INI set files, the configuration directory, and both resolution chains —
CLI-free, with 8 unit tests), `src/views.rs` (serializable view DTOs),
`src/handlers.rs` (`#[handler]` adapters), `src/main.rs` (clap surface,
`#[derive(Dispatch)]` command tree, `AppBuilder` wiring, 4 unit tests),
`src/templates/**` (8 MiniJinja templates, one per command path) and
`src/styles/default.css`.

Resolution happens once per invocation in a pre-dispatch hook registered on all
eight command paths; it builds a `Session` into `ctx.extensions`, so handlers
just read it. The two chains are kept separate in `Session::resolve`, and only
the active set's file is ever read, so nothing merges. Domain errors travel as
`ExternalFailure(1, "gcloudlike: …\n")`, which is what keeps the stderr payload
verbatim and the status at 1; usage errors (including malformed property keys,
which a clap `value_parser` rejects) stay clap's, at status 2.

Verified black-box against the produced binary with `check.sh` at the workspace
root: 89 assertions over argv → stdout/stderr/exit status, covering the
inventory, both chains and every precedence pair the spec names, set isolation,
the `active_config` file, INI parsing and the byte-preserving write, all five
domain errors, all seven usage errors, both forms and their conflict rule, and
`--quiet`. All 89 pass against both the debug and the release binary
(`pass=89 fail=0`), plus `cargo test` 12/12.

2. Which of the provided documentation files (under docs/) did you actually consult? List their paths. (text) <id:sources.docs>

Read in full:
- docs/index.md
- docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md
- docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md
- docs/guides/leveraging-standout.md
- docs/topics/output-modes.md
- docs/topics/error-handling.md
- docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md
- docs/topics/app-configuration.md
- docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md
- docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md
- docs/crates/dispatch/topics/execution-model.md
- docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md

Read in part:
- docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md (the "Unknown Style Tags",
  "Style Aliasing" and "Best Practices" sections)

Searched (grep) across all of docs/ for "quiet", "notice", "stderr", "escape",
"literal [", "unknown tag" and "marker"; the hits outside the files above were
in docs/topics/stability.md, docs/topics/passthrough.md, docs/topics/testing.md
and docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md, which I read only as those matched lines.

Not consulted: the input, pipe and seeker docs, the tabular and file-system
guides, topics-system.md, partial-adoption.md, app-state.md, the upgrade
guides, production-shaped-example.md.

3. Did you rely on anything beyond the provided docs/ — web search, prior knowledge of standout internals, other repositories or source code? Say exactly what, or answer 'none'. (text) <id:sources.external>

No web search, no standout source code, no other repositories. What I relied on
beyond docs/:

- General Rust/crate knowledge that is not standout-specific: clap 4 derive
  (`global = true`, `value_parser`, subcommand nesting, its exit status 2),
  serde, MiniJinja whitespace control (`{%- … -%}`) and `loop.last`, and
  serde_json's `preserve_order` feature plus cargo's feature unification — I
  added `serde_json = { features = ["preserve_order"] }` to `app/Cargo.toml`
  specifically so that the JSON standout emits carries my views' declared field
  order (`name`, `zone`, `machine_type`, `status`) rather than an alphabetical
  one. docs/ does not mention JSON key ordering either way.

- Black-box probing of my own built binary, where docs/ did not answer a
  question. Two answers came from probing rather than from a doc:
  (a) how to put a literal `[` in rendered output — I ran the binary with
  values `[compute]`, `[[compute]`, `\[compute]`, `[core/project]`, `[ compute]`
  and `[Compute]` and observed that `\[` is consumed as an escape while
  `[compute]` is treated as an unresolved tag;
  (b) that `Output::Artifact` with zero bytes and `allow_stdout()` really does
  leave stdout at 0 bytes while writing the report to stderr with exactly one
  trailing newline.
  Both are observations of the produced binary's behavior, not of standout's
  source.

4. Friction points, if any: for each, quote the exact command, error message, or doc passage that caused it. (text, optional) <id:friction>

(a) Literal square brackets in output. `config list` must print `[core]` and
the three notices must print `[core/project]`, `[staging]`, `[prod]`. My first
attempt printed the section name plainly and the run said, on stderr:

    Standout :: Warnings
      Unresolved style tag(s) degraded to unstyled text: compute, core

That warning alone breaks SPEC.md's "Every other command that exits 0 leaves
stderr empty", so it had to go. Nothing in docs/ documents an escape; I found
`\[` by probing. Note `[core/project]` needs no escape (the `/` disqualifies it
as a tag) but `[staging]` does, so the templates escape uniformly.

(b) There is no documented channel for a success notice on stderr, and
docs/topics/error-handling.md is explicit that a handler must not write one
itself: "Do not print or call `process::exit` from handlers. This keeps capture
APIs, `TestHarness`, output ownership, and real process behavior on the same

workarounds answer.

`CommandContext`." So the reconciliation had to happen before `app.run`, on

pre-dispatch hook gets:

    > matches they receive — is issue #352 in the adopter-seams epic.

correct under either answer.

docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md ("The engine consumes exactly one final

    | Output Mode | Behavior                    |

undefined `[compute]`: the tag was **not** stripped — `[compute]` came through
as literal text — and a framework warning was emitted to stderr, "Unresolved
style tag(s) degraded to unstyled text: compute". The behavior is friendlier
than the docs claim, but the stderr warning is invisible in the docs, and for
an application whose contract pins stderr that difference is the whole ball
game.

(b) Missing. No page documents how to emit a literal `[` from a template.
`\[` works (and suppresses the warning); docs/ never mentions it. The nearest
thing is docs/crates/render/topics/template-engines.md's table of *MiniJinja*

does not help with pass 2's BBParser.

policy — but there is no signature list, and nothing says whether an empty byte
vector is legal (it is), or whether the report is written with a trailing
newline (it is: exactly one).

(d) Missing. Nothing states how structured modes order object keys.

`name, zone, machine_type, status` serializes as `machine_type, name, status,
zone`. That is serde_json's default `Map`, and it is fixable only from the
application's own `Cargo.toml`, which is a surprising place to have to reach.

(e) Missing. docs/topics/output-modes.md says of `--output`: "The flag is
global—it applies to all subcommands", but nothing says whether a global flag
declared by the *application* is readable from the deepest `ArgMatches` that
`#[flag]` reads. It is (`#[flag] quiet: bool` works on a nested `config set`),
but I only learned that by running it.

6. Workarounds you left in the produced code, if any. (text, optional) <id:workarounds>

Four, all in the CLI layer, all commented at their site:

(a) `reconcile_output` in `src/main.rs` rewrites argv before `app.run`. When
`--format json` is present it drops any `--output …` token and appends
`--output=json`; when `--format text` meets a structured `--output` it appends

confined to lines that actually name both forms. `--format` is a real clap
flag (so `--format xml` is a proper usage error) and `--output` stays
standout's own. Four unit tests pin the rewrite, including that
`--output-file-path` is not mistaken for `--output`.

(b) `config set`, `configurations create` and `configurations activate` return

"artifact to stdout" destination, whose documented report channel is stderr.

one newline, exit 0 — and the notice's wording stays in a template rather than
in a handler, but the shape is being used for something it was not designed
for. Under `--quiet` these return `Output::Silent` instead.

rendered through the selected mode, `config set --format json` writes the

cargo's feature unification changes how *standout* serializes, giving the
machine projection the field order SPEC.md writes. The crate is never named in
the source. It is a lever pulled at a distance, so it is commented in the
manifest.

active set is resolved and checked for existence on every command, including
`configurations activate`. That follows "Naming a set that does not exist is a
domain error, whichever source named it", but it does mean a hand-edited
`active_config` naming a deleted set cannot be repaired with `activate` alone.

high

nothing effective — standout's `writeln!` edge means stdout is a single `\n`

`configurations activate` is the intended reading.

content.text:
Done. `gcloudlike` is implemented, verified, and the questionnaire is answered.

**What's there**

- `app/src/inventory.rs` — the three frozen rows, CLI-free.
- `app/src/settings.rs` — property keys, INI set files, the configuration directory, and both resolution chains. CLI-free, 8 unit tests.
- `app/src/views.rs`, `app/src/handlers.rs` — serializable view DTOs and `#[handler]` adapters.
- `app/src/main.rs` — clap surface, `#[derive(Dispatch)]` command tree, `AppBuilder` wiring, 4 unit tests.
- 8 MiniJinja templates + `styles/default.css`.

Settings resolution runs once per invocation in a pre-dispatch hook on all eight command paths, building a `Session` into `ctx.extensions`. Only the active set's file is ever read, so nothing merges. Domain errors travel as `ExternalFailure(1, …)` — that's what keeps the stderr payload verbatim and the status at 1 instead of standout's `Error: ` framing; usage errors (malformed keys included, via a clap `value_parser`) stay clap's at status 2.

**Verification** — `check.sh` at the workspace root: 89 black-box assertions over argv → stdout/stderr/exit status, covering the inventory, every precedence pair the spec names, set isolation, the `active_config` file, INI parsing and the byte-preserving write, all five domain errors, all seven usage errors, both output forms and their conflict rule, and `--quiet`. **89/89 pass against both the debug and the release binary**; `cargo test` is 12/12; `cargo build` is clean.

**Three things worth your attention**

1. **The stderr notices use `Output::Artifact` with zero bytes.** There is no documented channel for a success notice on stderr, and the docs forbid printing from a handler. An artifact whose destination is stdout has its report written to stderr — so an empty byte vector plus `allow_stdout()` yields exactly the spec's shape (stdout 0 bytes, stderr the notice, exit 0). It's the right effect through a mechanism built for something else.
2. **`--format` is reconciled on argv before `app.run`.** `AppBuilder` can rename or remove `--output`, not run a second flag beside it that wins. Only lines naming both forms are rewritten; everything else passes through.
3. **The docs are wrong about one thing I hit.** Both styling-system.md and templating.md say Text mode strips unknown style tags. It doesn't — it keeps them literal *and* writes a framework warning to stderr, which would have broken the spec's "stderr empty on success". The `\[` escape that fixes it is documented nowhere; I found it by probing the built binary. That's written up in the questionnaire's gaps answer.

I also added `serde_json` with `preserve_order` to `app/Cargo.toml` so the JSON carries the field order the spec writes rather than an alphabetical one — a lever pulled at a distance via cargo feature unification, so it's commented in the manifest.
